questions.question: Which of graphs A–D correctly shows $y=\dfrac{|x|}{x^2}$?
Which of the following is the constant term in the expansion of $\left(2x-\dfrac{5}{x^3}\right)^{12}$?
questions.answer: The general term has power $x^{12-4r}$, so $r=3$: $\binom{12}{3}2^9(-5)^3$.

The graph of $f(x)=x^2-4x+5$ is shown. Explain why $f(x)$ does not have an inverse function.
questions.answer: $f$ is not one-to-one: it fails the horizontal line test (for example $f(1)=f(3)$).

questions.question: Let $g(x)=x^2-4x+5$, $x\ge2$ (the right half of a parabola with vertex $(2,1)$). Sketch the graph of the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$.
questions.answer: Reflect $y=g(x)$ in $y=x$: a half-parabola starting at $(1,2)$, vertical there, increasing and concave down.

Three boys and five girls sit in a circle. Two particular boys are asked not to sit together. In how many ways can this occur?
questions.answer: Total minus those with the two boys together: $7!-2\times6!=5040-1440=3600$.

questions.question: Show that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\sin^{-1}(2x-1)\right]=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x-x^2}}$.
Hence, or otherwise, show that $\displaystyle\int_{3/4}^1\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x-x^2}}=\frac{\pi}{3}$.
Using the substitution $x=2\cos\theta$, evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^{\sqrt2}\frac{dx}{x^2\sqrt{4-x^2}}$ in simplest exact form.

The diagram shows part of the curve $C$: $y=2-\dfrac{1}{2x-1}$, $x\ne\dfrac12$. The region bounded by $C$, the lines $x=1$, $x=2$ and the $x$-axis is rotated about the $x$-axis. Show that the volume of the solid is $\pi\left(\dfrac{13}{3}-2\ln3\right)$ units$^3$.
Prove by mathematical induction that for integers $n\ge1$, $$\frac{3}{1\times2\times2}+\frac{4}{2\times3\times2^2}+\dots+\frac{n+2}{n(n+1)2^n}=1-\frac{1}{(n+1)2^n}.$$
questions.answer:
$n=1$: LHS $=\frac34$, RHS $=1-\frac14=\frac34$.

Assume true for $n=k$. Then
$$\text{LHS}_{k+1}=1-\frac{1}{(k+1)2^k}+\frac{k+3}{(k+1)(k+2)2^{k+1}}=1-\frac{2(k+2)-(k+3)}{(k+1)(k+2)2^{k+1}}=1-\frac{1}{(k+2)2^{k+1}}.$$
By induction the result holds for all $n\ge1$.

questions.question: A spherical weather balloon is inflated from empty so that its volume increases at a constant 0.5 m$^3$/s. Show that the radius at time $t$ is $r=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3t}{8\pi}}$ m.

A spherical weather balloon is inflated from empty so that its volume increases at a constant 0.5 m$^3$/s. The radius at time $t$ is $r=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3t}{8\pi}}$. Show that the rate of increase of surface area after 8 seconds is $\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}$ m$^2$/s.

The temperature $T^\circ$C of water in a kettle, $t$ seconds after it is switched on, satisfies $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=k(120-T)$ with $k>0$. The temperature is $20^\circ$C when switched on. Show that $T=120-100e^{-kt}$ satisfies the differential equation and the initial condition.

The temperature $T^\circ$C of water in a kettle, $t$ seconds after it is switched on, satisfies $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=k(120-T)$ with $k>0$. The temperature is $20^\circ$C when switched on. You are given $T=120-100e^{-kt}$. The kettle switches off at $100^\circ$C. If it takes 10 seconds to reach $30^\circ$C, find how long it takes to switch off, to the nearest second.
questions.answer:
$30=120-100e^{-10k}\Rightarrow k=-\frac1{10}\ln0.9\approx0.010536$.

$100=120-100e^{-kt}\Rightarrow e^{-kt}=0.2\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln5}{k}\approx152.8$.

It switches off after about 153 seconds.

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $|AB|=|BC|$ and $|CD|=|DA|$. $M$ is the intersection of $AC$ and $BD$, and $M$ bisects $AC$. Show that $\overrightarrow{BM}=\dfrac12\overrightarrow{BC}-\dfrac12\overrightarrow{AB}$.

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $|AB|=|BC|$ and $|CD|=|DA|$. $M$ is the intersection of $AC$ and $BD$, and $M$ bisects $AC$. Using $\overrightarrow{BM}=\dfrac12\overrightarrow{BC}-\dfrac12\overrightarrow{AB}$, prove that the diagonals of a kite are perpendicular.
questions.answer:
$$\overrightarrow{AC}\cdot\overrightarrow{BM}=(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC})\cdot\frac12(\overrightarrow{BC}-\overrightarrow{AB})=\frac12\left(|\overrightarrow{BC}|^2-|\overrightarrow{AB}|^2\right)=0,$$
since $|AB|=|BC|$. So $AC\perp BM$, and hence $AC\perp BD$.
